post_content:
Can a life coach help with anxiety? A coach doesn't diagnose anxiety or any other condition, although a coach can still be useful company for your thinking. Coaching is a conversation about your own choices and direction, and a coach is neither a mental health professional nor a provider of clinical care.

By anxiety, this answer means the ordinary worry or unease that most people recognise, and not a diagnosis. Achology sees it as an emotional state, and it teaches that people can build self-awareness and learn to regulate their feelings, though no coach can promise that growth on someone else's behalf.

How could a life coach help with anxiety of the everyday kind?

Picture the dread some people feel on a Sunday evening as a new week approaches. A coach would offer attentive company and ask questions, such as what you're telling yourself about Monday and whether that story is accurate and useful, so that you can see where you stand and decide what you'd like instead. That kind of conversation about your own choices and direction is what coaching is.

Where does a coach's role end?

In Achology's view, helping is education and never clinical care, so a coach does not diagnose or provide it, and Prospects, the UK's official graduate careers service, agrees that life coaches "are not qualified to diagnose or treat health, or mental health related issues". The line matters, and it applies to every coach.

The title coach on its own tells you nothing about a person's training. Asking any coach about their background, and about the ground their coaching does and does not cover, is a reasonable thing to do.

Does coaching suit what you want?

Anyone who wants to understand how their own thinking and feelings work can find that taught as education in Achology's courses, since Achology is a place to learn about the mind and not a clinic.

Achology steers clear of labels because it teaches feelings as something to understand and grow through, which is a different job from diagnosing them. For a fuller look at living with it, read Why Does Anxiety Feel Like It's Ruining My Life?

Which Achology courses teach life coaching?

Two courses cover it:

  • The Life Coaching Certificate Course (Beginner to Advanced) is taught online, and you can read about it on the Life Coaching Certificate Course (Beginner to Advanced) page.
  • The Life Coaching Blueprint: The Complete Process and Practices is also taught online, and you can read about it on the Life Coaching Blueprint: The Complete Process and Practices page.

Both courses are taught as applied psychology and as education, and neither gives you a clinical title.

So how long does it take to become a certified life coach? There's no single answer, because every provider decides how long its own certificate takes and no body sets a length that applies to all. Courses stretch from roughly eight weeks to three years, so a better question is how many hours a certificate demands and how many of your weeks those hours would fill.

Why do the lengths vary so much?

A certificate belongs to whoever awards it, which is why nothing is shared between providers. Life coach is a title that no country reserves and no organisation governs for the whole world, so no rule fixes how long the training should last.

Prospects, the UK's graduate careers service, lists an intensive eight-week course at one extreme and a three-year part-time master's degree at the other. Between them it places courses of 10 weeks, 38 weeks and nine to 12 months.

What does a well-known credential involve?

Take the Associate Certified Coach credential from the International Coaching Federation (ICF). A candidate needs 60 hours of coaching education, 100 hours of coaching experience of which at least 75 are paid, ten hours of mentor coaching across three months, and then a performance evaluation and an exam.

Teaching is therefore only one strand of that route, and the experience hours last as long as it takes you to find people to coach. Other bodies with voluntary credentials ask for different amounts, so these figures describe one route and not a universal measure.

Do hours translate into weeks?

Hours tell you how much teaching a course contains, and your own timetable settles the rest. A course of 10 swimming sessions tells you how many times you'll be in the water, yet how soon you feel safe in deep water depends on how often you return to the pool between them.

Divide the course hours by the hours you can spare weekly and you get the duration of the watching alone, so two people on one course can finish months apart without either doing anything wrong. Practice with real people comes on top, and how long Achology courses take explains how Achology's own courses fit your pace.

What should you put to a provider?

Ask how much of the course is teaching and how much is practice with feedback, since the two differ greatly. A course of mostly video can be completed fast and still leave little room to build the skill, and finishing a course is a different matter from showing a skill, so ask how the certificate is earned as well.

A good provider has both answers ready before you ask, and you can learn a lot from how clearly they give them. If the reply is vague, or only talks about how quickly you can finish, you'll know more about the course than a promise of speed could tell you. How a certificate is earned and how much practice sits beside the teaching are fair things to ask, and your own weeks are yours to plan around what you hear.

Is faster better?

Not necessarily, because a certificate records that a course was completed and can't show how well you coach. If you are weighing Achology against the ICF route, read the comparison with ICF certification first.

It costs little to try these ideas on your own life before committing, and doing so shows whether a longer training would suit you. In Achology's view, how long a course lasts matters less than what you do with it, because nobody can grow on your behalf.

What do Achology's life coaching courses offer?

Completing an Achology course earns a Certificate of Course Completion, and completing its six group sessions too earns a Certificate of Merit, Competency and Achievement. Neither is a professional qualification, as what your Achology certificate proves sets out in full.

Two life coaching courses are available:

  • The Life Coaching Certificate Course (Beginner to Advanced), with more than 38 hours of teaching, the figure to divide by your weekly hours.
  • Life Coaching Blueprint: The Complete Process and Practices, with over 31 hours.
